doc.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Young R&B artists she admires
summary: Brown names Oleta Adams, Toni Braxton, Aretha Franklin, Take 6 and James Ingram among artists she likes today.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: One last thing I would like to ask you. Who is coming up on the scene now as young R&B artists, that you think has their thumb on the pulse of great traditions.

Well I’ll tell you there’s a fine line now. A lot of the people that are being categorized as R&B singers, I don’t know. The category is strange and different now, you know? But I tell you, I admire Oleta Adams, wherever she’s been, I like her. I’ve heard some things by Toni Braxton, I like her a little bit. And I always slide back into Aretha on some things she just refuses to go away I say. When she’s right she’s just right. But there are a lot of the new artists that I’m not familiar with. I could talk to my daughter about that and she brings me up to what’s going on in the new voices. And there are those that I hear and can’t identify by name, you know. The music is still good. There are some things that don’t touch me but fortunately you can always turn the dial, you can take the compact disc out, you don’t have to be required to listen to it. I like groups like Take 6, I love them very much. And I like some of the things that BeBe and CeCe Winans are doing. I don’t know who else I can really touch on right now. I like Luther Ingram, is that his name? Luther Ingram?
Not Luther Vandross, I know Luther Vandross.
I went to high school with James.

You did? Yes. I like him. Of course now I listen to him and all you got to do is turn on Michael Bolton and you’ll hear all of his style. Michael Bolton’s doing it, thank you. But nonetheless, there are a lot of artists that I feel I maintain a lot of respect for. I like Luther Vandross also, you know, but I think if I had a preference I like James Ingram.
I’ll get word to James on that. He’ll appreciate and be flattered by that.
Would you do that? Okay. Thank you very much.
